newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kesko says expects to keep Anttila.
newsitem.headline: Kesko says expects to keep Anttila.

text.p: Finnish wholesaler and retailer Kesko Oy expects the EU to allow it to keep the Anttila retail chain after selling parts of its Tuko interest, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
Finnish radio news quoted CEO Eero Kinnunen as saying that Kesko plans to lower its market share elsewhere in order to be allowed to keep Anttila.
"Kesko can keep Anttila as long as its market share does not grow (from where it was before the acquisition of Tuko)," the spokesman said.
He said Kesko's share of the Finnish daily goods market before it bought Tuko was 40 percent and Anttila's market share was about two percent.
Kinnunen was not available to comment on the radio report.

Kesko said in a statement earlier that it wanted the European Commission to confirm that it would accept its sale of parts of Tuko to restore competition on the daily goods market, and allow it to keep Anttila.
The Commission blocked the merger of Kesko and its rival Tuko in November and Kesko announced earlier that it had agreed to sell parts of Tuko to a group of Finnish rivals.
